probes.statement: Avatar rejects null identity content.
probes.rationale: The runtime identity validator requires exactly one valid initials or local-source branch.

probes.statement: Avatar rejects unauthored adjacent size and presence tuples.
probes.rationale: The public union and runtime tuple list contain only the five authored combinations.

probes.statement: Avatar source evidence cannot be reordered to select a nearby branch.
probes.rationale: Registry verification preserves variant-container child order and exact record identity.

probes.statement: Avatar Group rejects zero direct identities outside the authored empty-slot branch.
probes.rationale: Populated group branches require fixed non-zero tuples.

probes.statement: Avatar Group rejects a singleton identity collection.
probes.rationale: The smallest authored populated group contains exactly two identities.

probes.statement: Avatar Group rejects null identities.
probes.rationale: Every tuple position is validated as a complete player identity.

probes.statement: Avatar Group rejects more than four direct identities.
probes.rationale: Overflow retains exactly four direct identities and represents the remainder as a positive count.

probes.statement: Avatar Group rejects zero and negative overflow counts.
probes.rationale: The overflow branch requires a positive integer.

probes.statement: Step Progress rejects arbitrary values outside 1, 2, 3, and complete.
probes.rationale: The closed value union and runtime guard share the same four authored states.

probes.statement: Avatar Group source record order stays stable.
probes.rationale: The immutable registry retains source index and variant-container ordering.

probes.statement: Avatar Group visible identity order remains caller order, including overflow meaning.
probes.rationale: A rendered aggregate semantic witness preserves the four names followed by the overflow count.

probes.statement: Player Item rejects missing required branch content.
probes.rationale: Each populated branch requires complete identity and branch-specific action data.

probes.statement: Player Item rejects null required content.
probes.rationale: Null identity data is outside the discriminated public contract and runtime validator.

probes.statement: Game Card rejects singleton participants and full-state cardinality mismatches.
probes.rationale: Open/default requires three participants and full action cards require four.

probes.statement: Game Card rejects arbitrary participant records.
probes.rationale: Participant objects use a closed identity shape and exact ascending slots.

probes.statement: Game Card rejects unsupported partial participant collections.
probes.rationale: Fixed tuples prevent silently padding or dropping partial collections.

probes.statement: Game Card rejects reordered participant slots.
probes.rationale: Runtime validation binds each array position to its authored slot.

probes.statement: Long Game Card content retains complete semantics and a reachable action.
probes.rationale: The constrained host render preserves long title and venue content; 200 percent native measurement remains Phase 5.

probes.statement: Notification Row rejects null branch content.
probes.rationale: Title, message, timestamp, read state, and action are explicitly validated.

probes.statement: Settings Row rejects missing branch content.
probes.rationale: Each row branch requires its authored label, value/state, icon, and callback shape.

probes.statement: Settings Row rejects unsupported icon, type, and state combinations.
probes.rationale: The discriminated branches prevent independent controls from manufacturing source-invalid rows.

probes.statement: Notification Row retains deterministic title, message, timestamp, and read-state order.
probes.rationale: The rendered accessible name fixes a coherent visible-order announcement.

probes.statement: Long row content does not lose its semantic value or action.
probes.rationale: Host boundary tests preserve complete names and values; native enlarged-text measurement remains Phase 5.

probes.statement: A numeric minimum score is not inferred by the display component.
probes.rationale: Revision 296 supplies display strings but no scoring-domain minimum, so the component deliberately does not calculate one.

probes.statement: A numeric maximum score is not inferred by the display component.
probes.rationale: The source does not define a maximum scoring rule and this milestone owns presentation only.

probes.statement: A result threshold is not inferred from score text.
probes.rationale: Explicit won, lost, or live state is authoritative because no threshold rule is present in the design evidence.

probes.statement: Caller-formatted score precision is preserved verbatim.
probes.rationale: Rendered semantic output preserves 6.000, 0006, 04, and 3.0 without numeric coercion.

probes.statement: Score rounding is not performed by the display component.
probes.rationale: Scores remain validated finite display strings and no arithmetic path exists.

probes.statement: Tie-breaking policy is not inferred from displayed sets.
probes.rationale: Revision 296 has no tie-breaking rule; consumers must supply an authored explicit result state.

probes.statement: Score Result Block rejects non-finite score text.
probes.rationale: NaN and positive or negative infinity spellings are rejected before rendering.

probes.statement: Score Result Block rejects arbitrary set counts.
probes.rationale: Each team owns exactly two score strings, matching the authored columns.

probes.statement: Score Result Block rejects missing teams.
probes.rationale: The public contract requires exactly two ordered team records.

probes.statement: Scores that could imply a tie do not create an unauthored result branch.
probes.rationale: Result state remains explicit and is never inferred from score equality.

probes.statement: Statistic and preference content rejects null display values.
probes.rationale: Presentational branches require non-empty textual content.

probes.statement: Score Result Block preserves team and set order.
probes.rationale: The aggregate summary follows team one then team two, with set one then set two.

probes.statement: Banner Toast rejects null message content.
probes.rationale: Title and message are required non-empty announcement strings.

probes.statement: Banner Toast rejects empty message content.
probes.rationale: Whitespace-only title or message values fail runtime validation.

probes.statement: Banner Toast rejects unsupported action and type pairs.
probes.rationale: Each semantic tuple owns exactly its authored close or view callback.

probes.statement: Repeated live-announcement churn remains a native-review backstop.
probes.rationale: Host tests prove stable announcement content and no timer; repeated native announcements require VoiceOver and TalkBack review.

probes.statement: Long Banner Toast messages retain the action and complete announcement.
probes.rationale: The constrained host render preserves semantics while native clipping measurement remains Phase 5.

probes.statement: Generic or invented Empty State copy cannot replace the human-approved strings.
probes.rationale: The exact five strings approved in Plan 04-08 are embedded and asserted.

probes.statement: Illustrated Card rejects null content and participant records.
probes.rationale: All copy and participant records are validated before render.

probes.statement: Illustrated Card rejects unsupported partial participant collections.
probes.rationale: Each branch requires exactly its authored two- or four-participant tuple.

probes.statement: Illustrated Card rejects missing callbacks on action branches.
probes.rationale: Every card type requires its single specifically named callback.

probes.statement: Empty State rejects callbacks on its no-action branch.
probes.rationale: No notifications exposes neither Create game nor Invite players.

probes.statement: Illustrated Card rejects unstable participant slot order.
probes.rationale: Participant positions must match exact ascending source slots.

probes.statement: Long Empty State and Illustrated Card copy keeps the authored action reachable without overlap.
probes.rationale: Host boundary stories and tests retain semantics and actions; 200 percent native measurement remains Phase 5.
